text:
John Tavares has played only 10 of Toronto's games, and those 10 have been rough for everyone. The Leafs have just 32% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, 17 points worse than without him, during a stretch when the whole team has sagged.

The bad luck is real, though. Toronto has scored about five fewer goals than its chances deserve with Tavares on, and he's shooting 9% against a range that usually sits around 14. Evolving-Hockey noted last season that he played with weak teammates and against top competition, which makes raw on-ice numbers look worse than his own effect. He still lives at the net: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 98th percentile for chances from the slot.

He's 36, with 1,185 career points, and since Kirill Marchenko went down he's moved onto William Nylander's line. He told Daily Faceoff Toronto he feels he needs to elevate his game. Our range has him at 44 to 67 points.
